subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Women's Petition Against Coffee
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Women's Petition Against Coffee.

hook.text: In 1674, London women published 'The Women's Petition Against Coffee,' complaining their husbands spent all day in coffeehouses.

buildup.text: The petition claimed coffee made men impotent, lazy, and absent from home. Wives were fed up with empty beds and cold dinners.

discovery.text: Men responded with 'The Men's Answer'—arguing that coffee improved their stamina and intellect, making them better husbands.

twist.text: The petitions were likely satirical—18th-century social commentary disguised as a gender battle. But the social tension was real.

climax.text: Charles II tried banning coffeehouses in 1675. The ban lasted just 11 days before public outcry reversed it.

punchline.text: Women protested, the king banned, the people revolted. Coffee was unstoppable.

quiz.question: How long did King Charles II's 1675 coffeehouse ban last?
options: Just 11 days before public outcry reversed it
